articles.headline: Cardinals' Budda Baker hopes to stay with Arizona at trade deadline
articles.description: Budda Baker hopes that when the trade deadline passes, he'll still be in Arizona.
articles.headlineJa: カージナルスのバッダ・ベイカー、トレード期限後もアリゾナへの残留を希望
articles.descriptionJa: バッダ・ベイカーは、トレード期限が過ぎた後もアリゾナに残っていたいと考えている。
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- Cardinals Pro Bowl safety Budda Baker hopes that when the trade deadline passes, he'll still be in Arizona.

Baker told ESPN on Wednesday that he has not requested a trade, nor has he requested not to be traded. Baker also said he has not talked to general manager Monti Ossenfort "about anything."

The NFL trade deadline is on Nov. 10.

"My approach is I'm here," Baker said. "I'm here. I want to win. I want to be here. And I'm just controlling what I can control, just taking it one week at a time, and hopefully when the deadline ends, I'll still be here. If not, I mean, it's a business. I understand at the end of the day and that's it."

Baker pointed out that his name has been attached to trade rumors for "like five, six years now."

"So, at the end of the day, I'm here, be where your feet are," Baker said. "I'm happy to be a Cardinal and just focus on getting a W this week versus Cowboys."

Baker, 30, is in his 10th season, all with the Cardinals. He made the Pro Bowl in eight of his first nine seasons, with the past seven coming at safety. He was named a Pro Bowler on special teams as a rookie.

Baker has eclipsed 100 tackles in six of his first nine seasons and is on pace for his seventh. He has nine career interceptions and 13.5 career sacks.

Baker is in the second season of a three-year extension that he signed toward the end of the 2024 season that is scheduled to keep him under contract through the 2027 season. Baker is scheduled to earn $16.17 million this season.

Baker said he understands that the NFL is, ultimately, a business and the trade deadline is a means to help teams improve.

"It's a deadline for a reason," Baker said. "Teams are trying to get players, and our team might be trying to get players and getting other players. So, at the end of the day, it's a business.

"So, for me, it's just continue to play great football. I feel like I'm playing great football right now and just control what I can control."

articles.headline: Bayern Munich's Vincent Kompany discharged from hospital after collapse
articles.description: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany has been discharged from the hospital following his collapse last week.
articles.headlineJa: バイエルンのヴィンセント・コンパニー、倒れた後に退院
articles.descriptionJa: バイエルンのヴィンセント・コンパニー監督は、先週の失神を受けて病院を退院しました。
articles.body:
Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany was discharged from hospital on Wednesday following his collapse last week.

The Bundesliga champions' director of sport Max Eberl told German broadcaster ARD that Kompany, 40, had been diagnosed with meningeal irritation after being admitted to hospital on Friday.

- Bayern honor Kane for Ballon d'Or win before German Cup rout

Eberl was speaking before Bayern's 6-1 thrashing of Magdeburg in the German Cup at the Allianz Arena on Wednesday night, five days after Kompany had collapsed while watching the club's second team train.

"Given the circumstances, he's doing ⁠well," Eberl said. "He ‌was discharged from the hospital [on Wednesday]. That is the biggest and best news for all of ‌us.

"It's a meningeal irritation that caused this incident on Friday. He will now rest and take medication and I am certain that he will ⁠very soon be back on the touchline, operating at 100 percent."

Eberl had said on Friday that it would be "weeks, not days" before the Belgian coach, who had been ill with a virus, would be able to return to work.

Harry Kane revealed after his Ballon d'Or win in London on Monday night that Kompany had telephoned him to wish him luck earlier that morning.

Kompany missed Saturday's 3-1 Bundesliga win at Freiburg, with assistant Aaron Danks taking charge of the ⁠team for that match and the cup win over Magdeburg.

Bayern are top of the Bundesliga table on goal difference, level on points with Borussia Dortmund who they play at home on Saturday.

Information from PA contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Justin Jefferson on down year amid Vikes' 6-0 start: 'What we're doing is working'
articles.description: Justin Jefferson, whose 23 catches are a career low through the first seven weeks of a season, said ultimately what the 6-0 Vikings are doing now "is working."
articles.headlineJa: ジャスティン・ジェファーソン、バイキングスが6戦全勝の好スタートを切る中で不調に言及：「今のやり方はうまくいっている」
articles.descriptionJa: シーズン最初の7週間で23回のキャッチというキャリア最低の数字に留まっているジャスティン・ジェファーソンだが、6勝0敗のバイキングスが現在行っていることは、最終的に「うまくいっている」と語った。
articles.body:
EAGAN, Minn. -- Minnesota Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson said Wednesday that "it's definitely an in-between feeling" as his production languishes while he plays for the NFL's only undefeated team.

As the Vikings (6-0) adjust to new quarterback Kyler Murray, Jefferson has had the worst start in his seven-year career. His 60.4 receiving yards per game through Week 7 is 32% lower than his next-worst start to a season in 2025, when he averaged 88 yards. His 23 catches are also his lowest total through the first seven weeks of a season in his career.

Jefferson has missed one full game and most of another because of a sprained left ankle, and the Vikings have already had their bye. He cited those mitigating factors Wednesday in saying that he is not "too frustrated or just going to the higher-ups and asking for the ball."

All told, 71 NFL players have more targets than Jefferson (31) this season.

"I definitely would love winning games over having that production," Jefferson said. "There was definitely years before where I had that production and was not winning games. So it's definitely an in-between feeling on, you want to be the best player in the league, and you want to have that production to show you are the best player in the league, but we're winning games and we're the only team undefeated in the league.

"What we're doing right now [as a team] is working. Obviously there's things to do better and things to fix on the offensive side of things, but all in all, it's coming together and we're doing things to win games."

The Vikings will enter the most difficult portion of their schedule beginning this week at the Detroit Lions, a game that will be followed by matchups against the Buffalo Bills, Green Bay Packers and San Francisco 49ers. To this point, coach Kevin O'Connell has worked to get Murray more comfortable in the offense, while knowing his team has the best defense in the NFL and one of the league's top special teams. O'Connell's solution: Through seven weeks, the Vikings have the NFL's fourth-highest rate of designed runs (43.3%) and its second-fewest number of dropbacks (198).

"In the past we were throwing the ball a thousand times," O'Connell said Wednesday when asked about the drop in Jefferson's production. "That's one thing. When you lead the league or you're close to in rushing attempts on the early downs, controlling the game or attempting to control the game, there may not be just the amount of volume [of throws]. But he's our best player. We've got to find a way to continue to activate him."

articles.headline: Ranked: Every Premier League team's money-per-points (after Man City cheated)
articles.description: How much did Premier League teams spend for points -- after Man City cheated? We find out which clubs were wasteful and which spent smart.
articles.headlineJa: ランキング：プレミアリーグ全チームの「勝ち点あたりの費用」（マン・シティの不正後）
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティの不正発覚後、プレミアリーグの各チームは勝ち点のためにいくら費やしたのか？無駄遣いをしたクラブと、賢明に投資したクラブを明らかにする。
articles.body:
A few weeks ago, when the Premier League announced that Manchester City were guilty of 114 different violations that added up to them illegally spending an extra $1 billion, everyone realized that the Premier League isn't actually fair.

How do we look back on that decade of soccer? What does it mean for Pep Guardiola's legacy? Or Jurgen Klopp's? Or any of the hundreds of other people who were affected in some direct or indirect way?

One team cheated, and that team has won six of the past nine Premier League titles. Oh, and they're currently in first place this season. Sports require some version of arbitrary integrity for them to make sense -- we currently don't have that.

Perhaps, more importantly, we don't even have the illusion of integrity right now.

Manchester City look like the best team in the league but we all expect some big punishment to be thrown at them any day now. But as I wrote about last week, the idea that the Premier League was fair before Manchester City were bought by Abu Dhabi United Group -- or that everyone else is still operating across an equal playing field -- was itself an illusion.

Last season, Arsenal won the Premier League with an estimated payroll of about €219.3 million, while Brentford had the league's smallest estimated payroll at €62.9 million. Outside of Leicester City's magical run in 2015-16, the team that wins the Premier League is always one of the richest teams in the Premier League.

So, as we continue to grapple with the meaning of what we've watched over the past decade, I wanted to look back on everything we've seen in a slightly different way: Who got the most out of what they spent? If everyone had roughly the same resources, who would've dominated the Premier League and who would've sunk to the bottom of the standings?

How we created the rankings

For this list, I looked at the last 10 full Premier League seasons, and I chose the 20 teams that played the most matches. Then, I gathered spending data from FBref, which has estimated wage data for every club, and Transfermarkt, which is the best public source for transfer spending data.

From there, I calculated the average total spending for every club in the seasons they competed in the Premier League. That total is just a combination of their average annual roster payroll and their average annual net transfer spending.

Finally, I took the total spending for each team and divided it by the number of points won in the Premier League standings -- a win being worth three points, a draw worth two.

That gives us the final metric to sort this list: millions of Euros spent per point won.

We'll start with the most efficient teams topping the list -- the teams that could shoot up the table if they were allowed to spend more money -- and, we'll continue down until we find the most wasteful teams that spent the most for the points they got.

1. Brentford: €1.2 million per point

articles.headline: Enzo Maresca: Man City 'never practiced penalties' before shootout win
articles.description: Man City boss Enzo Maresca said his players had not practiced penalties after edging past Brighton in a Carabao Cup shootout on Wednesday.
articles.headlineJa: エンツォ・マレスカ：マン・シティはPK戦での勝利前に「一度もPK練習をしていなかった」
articles.descriptionJa: 水曜日に行われたカラバオ・カップでブライトンをPK戦の末に僅差で破った後、マン・シティのマレスカ監督は、選手たちはPKの練習をしていなかったと語った。
articles.body:
Man City boss Enzo Maresca said his players had not practiced penalties after edging past Brighton in a Carabao Cup shootout on Wednesday.

City's back-up goalkeeper Gerónimo Rulli made two saves as the holders won 4-3 on spot-kicks to reach the quarterfinals after twice coming from behind in a thrilling 2-2 draw at the Etihad Stadium.

"To be honest, since I've been here we never practiced penalties," said Maresca before going on to praise the five players who did step up.

Phil Foden, Enzo Fernández, Jérémy Doku and Rayan Cherki were all successful while Mateo Kovacic's miss ultimately did not matter as Rulli denied Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk.

Maresca said: "We're very happy with the five, even Mateo. It always happens, the one that scored during the 90 minutes, and then misses the penalty."

Kovacic had cancelled out Malick Yalcouyé's opener before halftime but the impressive Georginio Rutter restored the Seagulls' lead after the restart.

Rutter then had a shot tipped onto the bar by Rulli and hit the side-netting as the visitors threatened to take complete control.

The game and the atmosphere changed after the introduction of Jeremy Doku from the bench and Vitor Reis diverted in a Cherki free kick to take the match to penalties.

- Man City survive penalties to advance past Brighton

- Gianluigi Donnarumma 'making mistakes,' defended by Man City boss Enzo Maresca

"I'm not sure he changed the game, but for sure he made an impact," said Maresca of Doku's introduction. "This is the reason why they are there -- when they start from the beginning, to try to do their best, and if they go on from the bench, to try to make an impact."

Maresca had no regrets about his decision to rest Erling Haaland, Gianluigi Donnarumma, Rúben Dias, Elliot Anderson and Josko Gvardiol after giving them brief holidays.

He said: "I was happy with the way we planned the game, with the rotation, and especially I was very, very, very happy with the ones that were playing."

Maresca, who made nine changes, praised Donnarumma's deputy Rulli.

He said: "Apart from the penalties, I think overall he was good, especially in the build-up. He also made a good save."

Brighton, who made seven changes themselves, will return to the Etihad in the Premier League on Saturday.

Manager Fabian Hurzeler said: "We lost in a shootout. We had enough chances to win the game but the goals we conceded were very unlucky.

"They had the luck today. We have to reset. We have a great chance on Saturday to take revenge.

"We will never blame players who miss chances or miss penalties. It is a team sport and we stick together. I saw a team who tried hard and a team who gave everything, also out of possession."

articles.headline: Bologna storm back to hand Milan, Amorim first Serie A loss
articles.description: Samuel Mbangula fired a hat trick as Bologna beat AC Milan 4-2 to hand the hosts a first Serie A loss of the season.
articles.headlineJa: ボローニャが猛追、ミランとアモリムに今季セリエA初の敗戦を喫させる
articles.descriptionJa: サミュエル・ムバンギュラがハットトリックを決め、ボローニャがACミランに4-2で勝利。ホームチームに今シーズンセリエAで初めての敗戦を味わわせた。
articles.body:
Samuel Mbangula fired a hat trick as Bologna beat AC Milan 4-2 to seal their first Serie A win at San Siro in over 10 years -- and hand the hosts a first league loss of the season.

Belgian forward Mbangula, on loan from Werder Bremen, opened the scoring and struck twice more after Milan defender Davide Bartesaghi's own goal had given the visitors a second-half lead.

Milan midfielder Alphadjo Cissè scored twice, cancelling out Mbangula's opener and then giving his side a halftime lead, but it was not enough as Ruben Amorim saw his team lose for the first time in Serie A since his arrival.

Bologna had won their previous two league games on the road and they silenced the home fans in the eighth minute when Mbangula converted from inside the box after being teed up by Nadir Zortea.

The visitors' lead was short-lived. Milan's on-loan Nottingham Forest winger Omari Hutchinson dispossessed Bologna defender Arthur Theate and squared for Cisse to steer in the equaliser.

Hutchinson then had a hand as Milan took a 27th-minute lead, driving into the box before Fikayo Tomori set up Cisse, who stabbed home his seventh goal of the season in all competitions at the back post.

Bologna boss Raffaele Palladino made a triple change on the hour-mark, sending on Juan Miranda, Nicolò Cambiaghi and Martin Vitík, and his side responded with two goals in as many minutes to turn the game on its head.

Bartesaghi diverted a free kick into the box past his own goalkeeper to level it up at 2-2 in the 60th minute and Mbangula lashed home his second from Miranda's assist.

Francesco Camarda and Sankhoun Diawara both headed narrowly wide for Milan as they chased a late equaliser, but Bologna sealed all three points on the counter-attack as Mbangula swept home Odgaard's cross for his hat trick.

Information from PA was used in this recap.

articles.description: AS Monaco and USMNT striker Folarin Balogun is reportedly linked with a move to Juventus. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.headlineJa: 移籍の噂・ニュース：ユヴェントス、米国代表のバロガン獲得を検討
articles.descriptionJa: ASモナコ所属で米国代表ストライカーのフォラリン・バロガンが、ユヴェントスへの移籍に関連付けられているとの報道がある。Transfer Talkが最新情報を伝える。
articles.body:
Juventus have made Monaco and USMNT striker Folarin Balogun their top priority for the January transfer window, while Paris Saint-Germain winger Désiré Doué has caught the eye of some top Premier League clubs. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Juventus have made Monaco striker Folarin Balogun their top priority for the January transfer window due to technical and financial factors, reports Tuttosport. The 25-year-old USMNT international is expected to leave Monaco after a €40 million summer move to Everton collapsed, while Atlético Madrid's Alexander Sørloth and Frosinone loanee Antonio Raimondo remain alternative targets for Juve.

- Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester City are monitoring Paris Saint-Germain winger Désiré Doué, alongside Bayern Munich, according to TEAMtalk. However, all the suitors face a setback in their hopes to sign him as PSG are progressing in talks over a contract extension with the 21-year-old France international to secure his future beyond 2029.

- Chelsea have focused their attention on signing AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott following their failed summer attempt, Florian Plettenberg reports. Liverpool are also looking to reunite Scott with Andoni Iraola, while TEAMtalk suggests the Cherries are targeting AZ Alkmaar's Kees Smit and Lazio's Kenneth Taylor as potential replacements for the 23-year-old England international.

- Chelsea, AC Milan, Galatasaray and Fenerbahçe are most keen on landing Brighton & Hove Albion midfielder Yasin Ayari, per TEAMtalk. Ayari, 23, has a deal that expires in the summer, though Brighton hold a one-year option to extend it which has created uncertainty around his future. The Sweden international has also been linked with Newcastle United, Arsenal, Manchester United, Liverpool, Atlético Madrid, Borussia Dortmund, Roma and Juventus.

- Former Manchester United winger Jadon Sancho has turned down an offer from Getafe after receiving a lucrative proposal from Saudi Arabia, according to Marca. The 26-year-old is a free agent and had requested a net salary of €3 million through the end of the season, which exceeded Getafe's financial capabilities.

OTHER RUMORS

- Chelsea remain admirers of Everton center back Jarrad Branthwaite, though the Toffees intend to keep him for the foreseeable future. (Football Insider)

- Chelsea, Manchester City, Arsenal, Tottenham Hotspur and Newcastle United all sent scouts to watch Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi score a hat-trick against Sint-Truiden. (TEAMtalk)

- Bayern Munich are monitoring Newcastle United loanee Nick Woltemade at Juventus as they evaluate a backup for Harry Kane. (Gazzetta dello Sport)

- Barcelona, Napoli, and Juventus are tracking Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Lucas Bergvall amid his limited first-team minutes this season. (TEAMtalk)

articles.headline: LaLiga chief Javier Tebas holds talks with Chinese ambassador over Mbappé-Mao controversy
articles.description: LaLiga president Javier Tebas has met with China's Ambassador to Spain, Yao Jing, to "find solutions" to the Kylian Mbappé alleged dictator comment.
articles.headlineJa: ラ・リーガのテバス会長、エムバペの毛沢東関連発言を巡る論争で中国大使と会談
articles.descriptionJa: ラ・リーガのハビエル・テバス会長は、キリアン・エムバペによる独裁者発言とされる問題の「解決策を見出す」ため、中国の駐スペイン大使である姚静（ヤオ・ジン）氏と会談した。
articles.body:
LaLiga president Javier Tebas has met with China's Ambassador to Spain, Yao Jing, to "find solutions" to the Kylian Mbappé alleged dictator comment.

Comments made by the Real Madrid striker regarding a "meme" comparing him to Mao Zedong, the founder of the People's Republic of China, sparked controversy in the Asian country.

EFE reported that Chinese state broadcaster CCTV suspended evening broadcasts of LaLiga matches and any games involving Mbappé.

"Today I held a meeting with the Chinese Ambassador to Spain to discuss the situation arising from Kylian Mbappé's comments and to seek solutions to move past this incident," Tebas wrote on X.

"Over recent years, LaLiga has worked closely with the Chinese authorities, football organisations, broadcasters and businesses in the country to promote the growth and popularity of Spanish football in China, while also contributing to the development and growth of Chinese football itself by sharing our experience, expertise and resources."

 

LaLiga has partnership deals with different Chinese organisations, including a strategic agreement with the Chinese Professional Football League (CFL) through 2029.

Moreover, it has agreements with China Media Group (CMG) for the growth of Chinese football and to bring "our competitions closer to millions of fans."

Tebas said he hopes the "single incident" does not affect their rapport.

"This is a relationship built on mutual respect, trust and cooperation, which we must preserve and continue to strengthen," Tebas wrote. "We are committed to continuing to work together to ensure that a single incident does not undermine the significant progress made or affect the millions of Chinese fans who follow our competitions. China is, and will continue to be, a strategic partner for LaLiga."

- Kylian Mbappé dropped by Chinese brands after alleged dictator comment

- Why Real Madrid's Mbappé, Barcelona's Yamal lost Ballon d'Or

- If Clásico win is any indication, Mourinho's Madrid might just be special again

At least three companies have cut ties with the France and Madrid star since his comment.

Mbappé issued an apology to the Chinese people on Tuesday on his social media, stating that his comment regarding Mao Zedong was "ill-judged."

Real Madrid, who own a percentage of Mbappé's image rights, also joined their player in apologising to the Chinese people.

"Real Madrid C.F. wishes to express its apologies to the Chinese people for any discomfort that may have been caused by the recent words of our player Kylian Mbappé," a club statement said on Wednesday.

"Our club holds deep respect for China, its history, its culture, and its citizens, as well as for the millions of Chinese fans who feel affection and admiration for Real Madrid."

articles.headline: Sources: USMNT's Christian Pulisic set to sign new AC Milan contract
articles.description: United States star Christian Pulisic is set to sign a new contract with AC Milan through to 2031, sources have told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者：米国代表クリスティアン・プリシッチ、ACミランと新契約を締結へ
articles.descriptionJa: 米国のスター選手クリスティアン・プリシッチが、2031年までのACミランとの新契約を締結する見通しであると、関係者がESPNに語った。
articles.body:
United States star Christian Pulisic is set to sign a new contract with AC Milan through to 2031, sources have told ESPN.

The deal for Pulisic, 28, is set to be announced in the next few days. Pulisic's deal was due to expire in June 2027, but a source has confirmed he has decided to extend for a further four years.

Pulisic joined AC Milan in 2023 from Chelsea for a fee in the region of €22 million ($24.4M). At the Serie A club, Pulisic has 44 goals and 28 assists across his 141 appearances and was the club's top scorer in the 2024-25 season.

Pulisic signed for Borussia Dortmund back in 2015 and established himself as one of the best young players in the Bundesliga. Chelsea signed him for £58M ($71.7M) in 2018 and there he won the 2021 Champions League.

But injury disrupted his progress at Chelsea and in 2023, AC Milan saw off competition from Juventus, Lyon and Galatasaray to sign him.

Pulisic missed most of AC Milan's preseason due to the injury he sustained during the World Cup. But after a steady reintegration into the first-team under Ruben Amorim, he has become an integral part of Amorim's Milan blueprint, playing in both the No. 10 role and on the wing.

At the international level, Pulisic has established himself as a key player for the USMNT with 33 goals in 90 appearances. He played in both the 2022 and 2026 World Cups for the USMNT and won the U.S. Soccer Male Player of the Year in 2017, 2019, 2021 and 2023.

articles.headline: Barcelona fined €602 over Julián Álvarez approach
articles.description: Barcelona have been fined €602 ($669) by the Royal Spanish Football Federation [RFEF] for approaching Julián Álvarez before notifying Atlético Madrid of their interest.
articles.body:
Barcelona have been fined €602 ($669) by the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) for approaching Julián Álvarez before notifying Atlético Madrid of their interest.

Barça plan to appeal the decision, a source said.

The Spanish champions made several attempts to sign Álvarez in the summer as they sought a new striker to replace the outgoing Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres.

Their pursuit of the Argentina forward angered Atlético, who accused Barça of making an illegal approach for the player and subsequently reported them to both the RFEF and FIFA.

FIFA declared it had no jurisdiction over the case, but the RFEF announced a small fine this week after finding Barça made contact with Álvarez's agent at the time, Fernando Hidalgo, before Atlético.

The RFEF's investigation established that a conversation took place between Hidalgo and Barça sporting director Deco on May 15, with the Catalan club's first written communication with Atlético following on May 28.

However, the infringement was only considered a "minor regulatory breach," with it falling under Article 133 -- instead of Article 93 -- of the RFEF's Disciplinary Code and, therefore, carrying a smaller punishment.

Article 93 is applied for "conscious and repeated breaches" of the RFEF's regulations.

Barça offered €100 million ($111m) for Álvarez and left the offer on the table until the end of the transfer window, but Atlético CEO Miguel Ángel Gil Marín repeatedly insisted they would not sell to their LaLiga rivals.

Atlético also turned down a €150m ($166m) offer from Real Madrid for Álvarez during the summer, with Arsenal and Paris Saint-Germain also expressing an interest in signing the forward.

Álvarez had revealed a desire to leave, telling ESPN during the World Cup that he felt a transfer would be best for all parties. Sources told ESPN he wanted to join Barça.

His push for a transfer saw him booed by Atlético fans at the start of the season, although bridges have started to be mended in recent weeks.

- Julián Álvarez apologizes to Atlético Madrid fans over bid to join Barcelona

- Why Real Madrid's Mbappé, Barcelona's Yamal lost Ballon d'Or

- Yamal excited despite Ballon d'Or miss: 'Good things take time'

The 26-year-old has scored in each of Atlético's last two games, against Stuttgart and Deportivo A Coruña, and after netting the winner in a 1-0 win against the latter on Saturday, he apologised to supporters.

"I wanted to say sorry to our fans for my comments during the World Cup," he told Movistar of his decision to speak out in search of a move.

"It was ‌a ⁠mistake -- the way I said what I said and the timing. I understand why the supporters are angry. If I were a fan, I'd be angry too. Especially given how they've supported me since I arrived."

Atlético have won eight of their opening 10 LaLiga games and are second in the table, just two points behind leaders Barcelona.
